# iru_in_house_app (Resource)

Manages an Iru In-House App (an `.ipa` for iPhone, iPad or Apple TV). The provider uploads the file at `source` and waits for Iru to validate it. A new upload happens only when the file's SHA256 changes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "iru_in_house_app" "field_app" {
  name   = "Field App"
  source = "${path.module}/FieldApp.ipa"

  runs_on_iphone = true
  runs_on_ipad   = true
  runs_on_tv     = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the library item.
- `source` (String) Local path to the `.ipa` file to upload.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the app is active.
- `runs_on_ipad` (Boolean) Install on iPad.
- `runs_on_iphone` (Boolean) Install on iPhone.
- `runs_on_tv` (Boolean) Install on Apple TV.

### Read-Only

- `app_identifier` (String) Bundle identifier read from the `.ipa`.
- `app_name` (String) App name read from the `.ipa`.
- `app_version` (String) App version read from the `.ipa`.
- `file_key` (String) Storage key of the uploaded `.ipa`.
- `file_size` (Number) Size in bytes of the uploaded `.ipa`.
- `file_updated` (String) Timestamp the `.ipa` was last uploaded.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the in-house app.
- `minimum_os_version` (String) Minimum OS version read from the `.ipa`.
- `sha256` (String) SHA256 of the uploaded `.ipa`, as reported by the API.
- `source_sha256` (String) SHA256 of the file at `source`, computed at plan time. A change triggers a new upload.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = iru_in_house_app.field_app
  identity = {
    id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the object in Iru.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = iru_in_house_app.field_app
  id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# In-house apps are imported by their ID.
terraform import iru_in_house_app.field_app 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
